script.title: Mastering Light: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments
script.subtitle: From reflection to complex lenses, master how light behaves and shapes our vision.

steps.body: Apply Law of Reflection: $\angle i = \angle r$ and light stays in the same plane.
Use Snell's Law: $n_1 \sin i = n_2 \sin r$ to find light's path change.
Apply Lens Maker's Formula: $\frac{1}{f} = (n-1)(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2})$ to find focal length.
Use Magnification $m = \frac{v}{u}$ for mirrors and $m = \frac{v}{u}$ for lenses.

script.example: An object is placed 20cm from a convex lens of focal length 10cm. Find image position. Using $1/v - 1/u = 1/f$: $1/v - 1/(-20) = 1/10 \implies 1/v = 1/10 - 1/20 = 1/20 \implies v = 20cm$. Answer: Real image at 20cm.
script.ctaBody: Solve the NCERT back exercises to solidify your ray diagrams.
script.videoPrompt: A single laser beam hitting a glass prism, splitting into a rainbow spectrum in slow motion.

topics.heading: Reflection and Spherical Mirrors
topics.explain: Light bounces off surfaces; spherical mirrors curve to focus light like a satellite dish. It follows the rule that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
bullets: Sign convention: direction of incident light is positive
topics.visual: A ray hitting a concave mirror and converging at a single focal point.

topics.heading: Refraction at Spherical Surfaces and Lenses
topics.explain: Light bends when moving between media of different densities, like a straw looking broken in water. This bending allows lenses to focus images.
topics.example: If $n=1.5$ and $R_1=R_2=\infty$ (plane), $f$ is infinite. For a lens, $n$ determines power.
topics.visual: A light ray passing through a glass slab and shifting laterally.

topics.heading: Refraction through a Prism
topics.explain: A prism bends light and splits it into colors because different colors bend at different angles. It is like a race where different runners (colors) take different turns.
topics.visual: A beam entering a triangular glass prism and emerging as a rainbow.

topics.heading: Optical Instruments
topics.explain: Devices like microscopes and telescopes use multiple lenses to magnify tiny or distant objects. They act like magnifying glasses for the whole world.
topics.example: Microscope with $f_o=1cm, f_e=5cm$ has $M = 1/5$ (ratio of focal lengths).
topics.visual: A cross-section view of a compound microscope showing two lenses and an eyepiece.

script.misconception: Students often confuse the sign convention. Remember: Distances measured in the direction of incident light are positive, and opposite are negative.
script.examTip: Always draw neat, labeled ray diagrams with arrows showing direction; marks are heavily allocated to the direction of light.
sources: NCERT Class 12 Physics: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments
